messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Competitive eval \u2014 model quality comparison & next tests

Thanks again for taking the call today, Alex \u2014 great to meet the SkyBank AI team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key priorities you called out:
- Minimize hallucination for regulatory Q&A (target: <= 5% on our bank-specific eval set)
- 95p latency goal for live queries under expected load (~300ms)
- Predictable unit cost and clear fallback strategy for peak traffic

What we propose for the next week:
1) Model quality run: Redwood-hosted baseline + 2 hyperscaler endpoints using your sample cases. We\u2019ll run the 500-case eval set (banking QA + hallucination probes). Attachment: eval_prompt_set_v1.csv.
2) Latency/throughput smoke: 50 concurrent virtual users, 95/99p latency and token throughput.
3) Security checklist: confirm PII redaction flow and audit log access for your compliance team.

Differentiators we\u2019ll highlight in the report: smart routing to dedicated pools, KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts, quantization profiles that preserve factuality, and rollout/fallback controls if we detect regressions. I\u2019ll attach an initial comparison PDF and the eval prompt set.

Please confirm: a) we should use your SkyBank test cases (you mentioned a curated set) or proceed with our eval set, b) whether you prefer Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated nodes for the latency run (we can do both).

If you\u2019re good with that plan, can we schedule a follow-up on Tuesday 11/24 to review preliminary numbers?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: eval_prompt_set_v1.csv
From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@skybank.com>

Thanks Marissa \u2014 appreciate the clear plan. Confirming we want the initial quality run against our own curated cases. I attached our current sample set (skybank_test_cases.csv) \u2014 contains 520 cases including regulatory Q&A, transaction anomaly scenarios, and red-teaming prompts we use to expose hallucination.

Two quick asks before you run: 
1) Can you include a per-case hallucination flag and a short explanation when a model hallucinates? That helps our compliance team triage.
2) For the latency smoke test, we want results for both Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated (if possible) \u2014 especially p95/p99 under burst load.

Also important: please confirm whether Redwood can redact account numbers automatically (we currently require deterministic masks in outputs) and which audit logs are available for the hosted option.

Proposed follow-up: Tue 11/24 works for us as a review.

Thanks,
Alex Jensen
Lead ML Engineer, SkyBank
alex.jensen@skybank.com

Subject: Fwd: Competitive eval \u2014 model quality comparison & next tests

Internal \u2014 forwarding Alex's set and initial pilot notes. I kicked off a baseline comparison between Redwood-hosted 'redwood-open-1' and the two hyperscaler endpoints Alex mentioned. Initial findings attached (skybank_eval_results_v1.csv) and a quick executive summary below: 

Executive summary (pilot run, 520 cases):
- Hallucination rate (case-level, defined as produced factually incorrect statements for closed-world banking queries):
  - Redwood-hosted (redwood-open-1): 4.1%
  - HyperscalerAPI-2: 7.8%
  - HyperscalerAPI-3: 9.3%
- Factuality / exact-match on regulatory Q&A: Redwood 82% vs 74%/69%
- Latency (hosted, small-scale): p95 = 285ms, p99 = 360ms (note: p99 affected by cold-starts and tokenization differences)
- Cost (token-cost normalized): Redwood baseline comparable to HyperscalerAPI-2; potential 15-20% cost reduction with quantized dedicated profile + caching.

Notes and next steps I recommend: 
1) Regression run: expand to 2k prompts (includes more red-team cases) to stabilize hallucination estimate.
2) Hallucination analysis: attach per-case failure reasons (prompt sensitivity, hallucinated entity, incomplete system prompt). Need Neha to confirm compliance language and whether per-case explanations are shareable.
3) Dedicated performance run: Aditya \u2014 can you run Redwood Dedicated with batching config (see attached redwood-dedicated-test-config.yaml) and replicate the latency/throughput smoke? Please capture p50/p95/p99 and concurrency scaling at 25/50/100 clients.
4) Quantization/regression: run the 8-bit quantized variant on 500-case subset to validate hallucination delta.

Attached: skybank_eval_results_v1.csv, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf, redwood-dedicated-test-config.yaml

Marissa

Thanks Marissa \u2014 I\u2019ll run the Dedicated tests this week. Plan and ETA: 
- Tests: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), and concurrency scaling at 25/50/100 clients for the 520-case set, then a 2k-run if results look good. Also run the 8-bit quantized variant on the 500-case subset (will capture hallucination delta).
- Config: using redwood-dedicated-test-config.yaml (attached). Will enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts to show cost/latency improvements.
- Expected artifacts: 1) storm-run logs (latency histograms), 2) per-case hallucination flags with short explanation, 3) cost-estimate delta between hosted/dedicated/quantized.
- ETA: baseline Dedicated run complete by 2026-11-23 EOD, 2k regression by 2026-11-27.

I\u2019ll upload results to the HubSpot deal and share Drive links; will include the exact commands and config so SkyBank can reproduce.

Aditya
